title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market
one_line: A 5-minute opening range breakout restricted to 'stocks in play' (top-20 relative volume at the open, price > $5, ADV ≥ 1m, ATR > $0.50), stop at 10% of ATR, exit at the close, 1% risk per trade, 2016-2023.

findings.statement: Universe: all US stocks; daily screen for top-20 relative volume (opening-range volume vs 14-day average ≥ 100%).
Entry: stop order at the 5-minute range high (if the first 5 minutes were up) or low (if down); stop 10% of 14-day ATR; exit at the close.
findings.evidence: Size so a stop loses 1% of capital, max 4x leverage.

findings.statement: Authors report ORB works far better on stocks in play than on all stocks.
findings.evidence: Results not visible in the summary read.

why.pattern: News/attention: unusually high opening volume marks stocks with fresh information and order imbalances that persist through the day.

reported_results.headline: Stocks-in-play ORB beats ORB on all stocks (per authors).

tradable_edge: Stocks only — not testable on our data. Index angle: use 'relative opening volume' on ES as an 'index in play' filter for ORB tests (T5 in the volatility study).
angles: ES relative-volume filter on the 5-minute ORB

decay_risk.reason: Published 2024 with a large retail following.

data_fit: No single-stock data in the inventory.
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 2), not by the weekly pipeline.
